subsystems.name: Soft continuum body
subsystems.role: flexible shaft that bends along winding vessels without damaging walls.

subsystems.name: Actuation
subsystems.role: makes the body bend and steer; two main routes are fluidic and electro-active.

subsystems.name: Sensing and shape estimation
subsystems.role: tells the surgeon where the tip is and what force it applies.

subsystems.name: Control and teleoperation
subsystems.role: translates surgeon input into safe, precise motion.

subsystems.name: Imaging integration
subsystems.role: lets the robot be seen inside the body.

subsystems.name: Therapeutic tip
subsystems.role: does the actual work — grasping, cutting, ablating or delivering therapy.

buildSteps.title: Design the continuum structure
buildSteps.detail: Define bending segments, stiffness and channel layout using models of the target vessels.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the soft body
buildSteps.detail: Cast medical-grade elastomer in moulds, or 3D-print it, embedding channels or EAP layers as it forms.

buildSteps.title: Build the actuators
buildSteps.detail: For fluidic versions, create sealed micro-channels; for EAP versions, deposit compliant electrodes on dielectric elastomer or ionic polymer films.

buildSteps.title: Integrate sensors
buildSteps.detail: Embed fiber Bragg gratings or strain gauges along the body and place a force sensor at the tip.

buildSteps.title: Add the therapeutic tip
buildSteps.detail: Mount micro-tools, cameras, laser fibres or electrodes on the distal end.

buildSteps.title: Connect drive and control
buildSteps.detail: Link the body to pumps and valves, or high-voltage amplifiers, and write control software with safety limits.

buildSteps.title: Test in phantoms and animals
buildSteps.detail: Navigate silicone vessel phantoms and then animal models to measure reachability, force and tissue damage.

buildSteps.title: Prepare for clinical trials
buildSteps.detail: Sterilise, package and run the regulatory safety studies needed for first-in-human use.

prerequisites.why: medical-grade silicones and elastomers are already used in catheters and implants.
moulding and 3D printing can make channels and EAP layers, but repeatability and miniaturisation remain difficult.

prerequisites.tech: Shape and force sensing in flexible bodies
prerequisites.why: fiber Bragg grating sensors work in labs, but integrating many into a millimetre-scale catheter is not routine.
kinematic models exist, but controlling a soft body under unpredictable tissue contact is still hard.
many EAPs need hundreds to thousands of volts, which is unsafe and bulky for a clinical device.
MRI-safe and fluoroscopy-visible soft robots are demonstrated but not standard.

pathway.milestone: research prototypes and early clinical trials of steerable soft catheters
pathway.unlocks: proof that soft robots can reach and treat specific anatomy safely.

pathway.milestone: first regulatory approvals for soft robotic tools in niche procedures
pathway.unlocks: commercial use in cardiology, gastroenterology or bronchoscopy.

pathway.milestone: integration with real-time 3D imaging and haptic feedback
pathway.unlocks: more precise, intuitive surgery in complex anatomy.

pathway.milestone: semi-autonomous or autonomous navigation inside the body
pathway.unlocks: procedures in remote or emergency settings, and reduced surgeon fatigue.
